kept: The paper's full mechanism chain, now including the two stages the previous revision omitted: section 2.1 preprocessing (industry-median then pool-median imputation -> 3xMAD outlier rule -> Z-score -> regression residual centering on industry dummies + market capitalisation, industry centering only for market-cap factors) -> LASSO screening of the second-level indicators -> EWM synthesis exactly as eq (1)-(5) print, with the min-max and entropy pool s in [t-12, t-1] EXCLUDING the decision month and the decision-month value z_ijt left unclipped -> Ridge / MLP / Random Forest each retrained monthly on tau = t-12..t-1 with a 1-month out-of-sample test (Algorithm 1) -> dynamic combination by IC_Mean, w_i = max(mu_IC_i, 0) / S over the trailing L = 20 monthly Spearman ICs, S = 0 -> w = 0 (Algorithm 2). Combined predicted return = the cross-sectional score.
changed:
(0) WHAT THE PREVIOUS REVISION GOT WRONG AND IS NOW THE PAPER'S. 0a EWM WINDOW ENDPOINT. eq (1) subscripts are s in [t-12, t-1], b in [1, N]: the min/max pool excludes the decision month t and only the numerator x_ijt is the current month. The previous revision pooled slots [mi-11, mi] (lag 0 included), which made v01 identically confined to [0,1], made its own declared clip unreachable, and erased the level information 'where does this month's cross-section sit against the trailing range'. Now: pool = slots [k-12, k-1]; one (lo, hi) pair per (indicator, decision month) shared by the pool and by month k; z_ijk = (x_ijk - lo)/(hi - lo) is NOT clipped and routinely leaves [0,1]. First valid decision slot = 13, matching 'rolling monthly advancement starting from month 13'. 0b ENTROPY WINDOW ENDPOINT. eq (2) denominator and eq (3) sum both run s = t-12..t-1, so w_ijt never sees month t; the previous revision's trailing-sum reducers included lag 0. Fixed with the same window. Also: eq (3)'s pool is now scaled by ONE (lo, hi) for the whole window, so sum p ln p = S2/S1 - ln S1 is an exact algebraic rearrangement of eq (2)-(3), not the approximation the previous revision declared under C1; the previous per-month-self-scaled pooling is gone. 0c INDUSTRY AND MARKET-CAP RESIDUAL CENTERING, previously absent entirely. section 2.1: 'each style factor is regressed on industry dummies and market capitalization, and the residuals from the regression are retained as the adjusted factor values' with 'For factors inherently related to market capitalization (e.g., the market capitalization factor itself), only industry centering is performed'. Now implemented per decision month by Frisch-Waugh (industry-demean the factor and the market-cap regressor within Sector, then regress one on the other) -- algebraically identical to OLS on industry dummies + market cap. Applied to every indicator except the four Size-group indicators, which get industry centering only. 0d MISSING VALUES NO LONGER DROP A STOCK. section 2.1 imputes a missing factor with the Shenwan industry median and, when that is unavailable, 'the overall median of the stock pool' -- the paper never deletes a stock for missingness. The previous revision dropped the indicator row on is.finite() and then deleted the whole stock-month on complete.cases. Now the full (pool x indicator) grid is materialised per month and imputed by industry median then pool median; what gets dropped is an INDICATOR with no observation at all that month, never a stock. 0e DUPLICATE INDICATORS REMOVED AT THE ROOT. The previous revision put M11_ST_Reversal and M29_Mom_5d (258/258 months bit-identical, DUPC-033) in one group, double-counting a 5-day reversal in the entropy weights. The Reverse group is no longer mapped onto registry momentum factors at all (see 0f); on the fundamental side FDB_MAP uses every registry factor EXACTLY ONCE, the connector is called with dedup = TRUE so the registry's own alias declarations collapse first, and a structural check dcasts the finished panel and drops any column that is numerically identical to an earlier one (logged). R18_Book_Leverage, D60_Leverage and Q15_Debt_to_Equity were deliberately NOT used because their registry definitions are sign-flips / near-restatements of Q16_Debt_to_Assets and Q13_Fin_Leverage. 0f HALF-LIFE AND SKIP-MONTH FIXED BY BUILDING THE PAPER'S OWN DEFINITIONS. Table 1's Roe20/Roe60/Roe120 are 'index-weighted cumulative daily rate of return, with a half-life of 60 trading days' and include the most recent month; the previous revision mapped them onto M04_Mom_1 / M03_Mom_3_1 / M02_Mom_6_1, which are equal-weighted and carry a 1-month skip -- the skip removes exactly the month a reversal factor lives in. The four price/volume/market-cap groups (size, reverse, volatility, liquidity) are now computed from RAWDATA to the paper's own definitions: exponential weights 0.5^(i/60) over 20 / 60 / 120 trailing trading days, no skip. 'Index-weighted' is read as exponentially weighted (指数加权), consistent with the same phrase in the Volatility group definitions. 0g FEATURE SET IS NOW AS-OF. The previous revision fixed the first-level group set once from the WHOLE panel and then skipped any month missing one of those groups, so late-arriving data retroactively deleted early months. Now the group set is taken per decision month from slots [k-12, k] only, and a month is never skipped for a missing group -- the model simply runs on the groups present (minimum 2).
(A) UNIVERSE / SAMPLE. A1 CSI 300 -> K200 union KQ150, PIT time-varying membership read from the signal-date RAWDATA row (harness axis). A2 sample: paper pool 2018-01..2022-12 with backtest 2020-01..2022-12; here the burn-in panel is attempted from 1996-01 over whatever months are available and scoring begins after the 12-month EWM window + 12-month training window + the first IC, graded by the harness from 2005-01. A3 liquidity floor adv20 >= 2e8 KRW at t-1 (harness axis, not in the paper), computed as shift(frollmean(Close*Vol, 20), 1) by ticker. A4 the paper's ST / suspended exclusions are mapped to the RAWDATA flags AdminStock / TradingHalt / UnfaithfulDisc read at the signal date; values that are not affirmatively true (NA, unparsable, absent column) count as NOT flagged -- lenient, because these flags are absent in early vintages and excluding on NA would delete whole early periods. A5 the paper's 'newly listed within the past month' is implemented directly as >= 20 prior trading rows for that ticker in RAWDATA (the previous revision implemented it as a side effect of the liquidity window). A6 ADDED BY ME, NOT IN THE PAPER: a pool stock must have a finite positive market cap at the month-end, because market cap is the regressor of the section 2.1 residual centering. A7 industry = the RAWDATA Sector column (paper: Shenwan Industry Classification Standard); NA / empty Sector is bucketed as 'UNKNOWN', which then triggers the paper's own pool-median fallback for imputation. If RAWDATA carried no Sector column at all, industry centering would degenerate to a global mean (logged, not silently).
(B) WHICH SECOND-LEVEL INDICATORS EXIST. B1 Table 1 lists 50 second-level indicators (37 survive the paper's LASSO); 31 are built here, under the PAPER's own names so every column is traceable to Table 1. NOT available and deliberately NOT proxied: Sm / Md / Lg / Elg (small/middle/large/extremely-large order money-flow reversal -- needs intraday order-size tape, which this infrastructure does not hold), IR_industry_pb and IR_industry_ps (need a daily P/B and P/S level series; the Factor DB exposes monthly z-scores only), Total_mv is kept but Rtop / Epstop / Pe are dropped because the only available registry analogues are reciprocals of factors already used for other Table 1 slots and reusing them would create exactly the bit-identical duplication of 0e, Basic_eps_yoy, CGR_eps, CGR_revenue_ps, IR_revenue_ps, CGR_mlev, CGR_dtoa, CGR_blev, IR_mlev, IR_dtoa, IR_blev (5-year compound-growth and 5-year information-ratio variants, not in the Factor DB). Per-group counts built vs paper: size 4/4, reverse 7/11, volatility 4/4, liquidity 4/4, earnings 2/4, growth 5/9, valuation 2/5, leverage 3/9. B2 SOURCE SPLIT. The four price/volume/market-cap groups are computed from RAWDATA to the paper's definitions and therefore carry the PAPER's own sign, un-aligned, as in the paper. The four fundamental groups come from load_month_factors() as Z_Score_Aligned (C15 gate, C13) and are therefore ALREADY direction-aligned by the connector's expanding Usable_Date <= sig_date IC path. This is a real asymmetry: inside a first-level factor, eq (5) sums w_ij z_ij, so aligning the sign of an individual indicator changes the group aggregate (it makes the fundamental composites all-good-direction, whereas the paper's aggregate mixes signs and lets the models learn direction). It is forced by C13 and is not something the paper does. B3 the fundamental values additionally arrive already z-scored upstream; the section 2.1 chain (impute / MAD / z / residualise) is applied on top of them uniformly with the self-built indicators, so for those twelve the MAD and Z-score steps act on an already-standardised input. B4 connector coverage_min stays at its default 0.05, so a thin indicator is dropped by the connector for that month and the group renormalises over the rest. B5 dedup = TRUE is passed to load_month_factors(), so a requested registry factor can be collapsed away as an alias in some month; it then simply is not present that month.
(C) SELF-BUILT INDICATOR DEFINITIONS -- choices the paper does not fully pin down. C1 Roe20/60/120: windows 20 / 60 / 120 trailing trading days from the factor names, which agree with the 'one-month / three-month / six-month' descriptions; weights 0.5^(i/60) with i = 0 at the signal day; computed on SIMPLE daily returns ('daily rate of return'); unnormalised. The normalisation choice is immaterial: dividing by sum(w) is a cross-sectionally constant affine map and the next step z-scores, so normalised and unnormalised give identical values. Log vs simple returns is NOT immaterial and simple was chosen. C2 non-finite daily returns are treated as 0 inside the exponentially weighted sums; a ticker with fewer rows than the window has the factor undefined. C3 Pct_chg / Turnover_rate / Amplitude / Vol: Table 1 says only 'if the stock <x> is less than the market average, multiply the return by -1' and gives no window. Implemented as the stock's trailing 20-trading-day compounded return, sign-conditioned on a cross-sectional comparison of <x> against the pool mean of <x> in that decision month. 20 trading days is the paper's OWN month length (Roe20 = 'one-month'). <x> = that same 20-day return / mean daily turnover rate / mean daily amplitude / mean daily share volume. Note these four are collinear by construction (all four have absolute value equal to the same return) -- that is the paper's own construction, and the paper's LASSO screened its Vol column to weight 0.000. C4 turnover rate = Vol * Close / Size, i.e. volume divided by shares outstanding recovered as Size / Close; guarded on Size > 0 and Close > 0. C5 amplitude = (High - Low) / previous Close, averaged over the window; the paper does not give the amplitude formula. C6 compounded returns use log1p with the daily return floored at -0.99 to keep log1p finite (ADDED numerical guard; a true -100% day would otherwise produce -Inf). C7 Beta / Std_e: weighted time-series regression of the stock's daily return on BM_Ret over 250 trailing trading days with the same 0.5^(i/60) weights. The paper says 'index-weighted' but states no half-life for the Volatility group and no regression window; 250 trading days is the only window it states in that group (Std_g, Dastd) and 60 trading days is the only half-life it states anywhere (Table 1 Roe), so one weighting scheme is carried across the two groups rather than inventing a second. If an auditor prefers the alternative, it is equal-weighted OLS over 250 days. Std_e = weighted residual sd = sqrt(max(var_y - beta*cov_xy, 0)). C8 Std_g = weighted sd of daily returns over 250 days; Dastd = weighted sd of daily EXCESS returns (stock minus benchmark) over 250 days. The paper's Dastd says 'excess returns' without naming the benchmark; BM_Ret is used. C9 ADDED: a weighted window must have at least 50% of its total weight observed (AX_MIN_WCOV) or Beta / Std_g / Std_e / Dastd are undefined; the paper imposes no such requirement. C10 Total_mv = Size; Total_mv_log = log(Size); Total_mv_3 = Size^3. 'Total market value in cubic meters' is read literally as total market value CUBED; the CNE5 alternative (cube of standardised log size, NLSIZE) was NOT used. The paper's own LASSO gave this column weight 0.000. C11 IR_industry_total_mv and IR_industry_turnover_rate: Table 1 says 'industry excess IR, with a time window of 20 trading days' and does not define IR. Implemented as mean / sd of the stock's daily industry-demeaned series over the trailing 20 trading days -- industry-demeaned log market cap and industry-demeaned turnover rate respectively. Daily industry means are taken over the K200 union KQ150 member panel present that day (not over the eligible pool). C12 Turnover_month / Turnover_quater / Turnover_year = mean daily turnover rate over 20 / 60 / 250 trailing trading days, using the paper's own month and quarter lengths and its stated 250-day year; note 12 x 20 != 250 is an inconsistency inside the paper's own conventions. C13 all trailing windows count the TICKER's own trading rows, so a halt shortens calendar coverage.
(D) FUNDAMENTAL MAPPING -- paper slot -> registry factor, each used exactly once. D1 Etop (net profit / total mv) -> V02_EP (NetIncome / MarketCap): exact. D2 Cetop (operating cash flow / total mv) -> V03_CFP (OperatingCF / MarketCap): exact. D3 Ps (price-to-sales) -> V08_PSR (MarketCap / Revenue): exact. D4 Pb (price-to-book) -> V01_BM (TotalEquity / MarketCap) = the RECIPROCAL of the paper's Pb. Monotone-decreasing, and the connector's direction alignment handles sign, but 1/x and x do not have the same cross-sectional shape, so the MAD bounds and z-scores differ from the paper's. D5 Dtoa (total debt / total assets) -> Q16_Debt_to_Assets: exact. D6 Mlev (paper: (total mv + non-current liabilities) / total mv) -> R17_Market_Leverage = -(TotalDebt / MarketCap): same market-leverage quantity, but TOTAL debt instead of non-current liabilities and reciprocal-signed. D7 Blev (paper: (net assets + non-current liabilities) / net assets) -> Q13_Fin_Leverage = TotalAssets / TotalEquity = 1 + TotalLiab / TotalEquity: same family, but TOTAL liabilities instead of non-current only. D8 Netprofit_yoy -> GR02_Earnings_Growth (YoY net income): exact. D9 Ocf_yoy -> GR06_OCF_Growth (YoY OCF): exact. D10 Or_yoy -> GR01_Revenue_Growth (YoY revenue): exact. D11 Roe_yoy -> GR05_ROE_Growth, whose registry definition is '5Y growth in NetIncome / Equity' -- a FIVE-YEAR horizon where the paper asks for year-over-year. Used because it is the only ROE-growth indicator available; the horizon mismatch is the deviation. D12 IR_eps (5-year EPS information ratio) -> Q07_Earnings_Stability ('1 - sd(earnings changes over 5 years) / mean(|earnings changes|)'): same 5-year earnings-stability family, different functional form. D13 NOT ADDED even though available: GR04_GPA_Growth, Q33_Earnings_Persistence, V07_EV_EBITDA, V10_FCF_Yield, V11_Shareholder_Yield, V13_EV_Sales, V16_Tobins_Q, S01_Size, S02_Float_Size, L26_Log_MktCap -- these have no Table 1 counterpart (or duplicate one already filled), and adding indicators the paper does not have would be as much a deviation as dropping its own.
(E) SECTION 2.1 CHOICES. E1 3xMAD: the paper states the rule ('observations exceeding three times the MAD from the sample median are treated as outliers') but NOT the treatment. Winsorising to median +/- 3*MAD was chosen over deletion, because the paper's own design never deletes a stock. MAD is the unscaled median absolute deviation (no 1.4826 factor). E2 ADDED guard: when MAD = 0 the rule would collapse the entire cross-section onto the median, so winsorisation is skipped for that indicator-month. E3 an indicator whose within-month sd is 0 (or below 1e-12) is dropped for that month, since the Z-score step is undefined. E4 the residuals are NOT re-standardised after centering -- the paper says the residuals themselves 'are retained as the adjusted factor values'. E5 a singleton industry gets residual exactly 0; that is a property of OLS on industry dummies, not a guard I added, and no minimum industry size is imposed. E6 ADDED guard: if the industry-demeaned market-cap regressor has zero within-month variance, its slope is set to 0 (industry centering only for that indicator-month). E7 the imputation / MAD / z / centering steps all run within one decision month's pool only -- no statistic crosses a month boundary.
(F) EWM CHOICES. F1 eq (3)'s normaliser is printed as ln(12 N) for a 12 x N pool; N varies month to month here, so ln(n) with n the ACTUAL pooled observation count is used -- the generalisation that keeps e in [0,1]. F2 0 * ln 0 := 0. F3 an indicator whose window pool is degenerate (hi - lo <= 1e-12) is excluded for that decision month and eq (4) renormalises over the rest. F4 ADDED numerical guard: w_raw = max(1 - e, 0). Mathematically e <= 1 always holds (entropy of a distribution over n cells against normaliser ln n), so this clamp is unreachable except for floating-point rounding -- declared rather than left silent. F5 eq (4) is normalised over the indicators actually present for that stock-month; if every weight in a group is 0 (perfectly uniform pool, every e = 1) the group falls back to the simple mean of its z values. The paper does not address either case. F6 a pool with only one observation is skipped (ln(1) = 0 divides).
(G) SCREENING. G1 the paper reports one screening (50 -> 37) and states neither the window nor a refit cadence; a single full-sample screening would violate PIT C1, so LASSO is refit MONTHLY on the same rolling 12-month training panel that Algorithm 1 uses. G2 the LASSO design matrix is the section 2.1 ADJUSTED values (the paper selects in section 2.3 before it synthesises), target = the monthly label. The paper does not state the LASSO target. G3 lambda = 5-fold cv.glmnet lambda.min, fold assignment seeded; the paper states no lambda and no CV scheme. G4 ADDED: an indicator absent from some slot of the training window is filled with 0 in the LASSO design matrix only -- 0 is the cross-sectional mean of a Z-score. The eq (5) aggregation does NOT use this fill; it renormalises instead. G5 zero-variance columns are dropped; if fewer than 2 columns survive, the month emits nothing. G6 screening may not delete a whole first-level factor: a group left with no survivor falls back to every indicator it has in that window, because the paper's model always keeps 8 first-level inputs. If cv.glmnet errors, all indicators are retained for that month. G7 the survivor set chosen at decision month k is applied to the whole training window AND the test month, which is the consistent reading of a one-off screening under a monthly refit.
(H) MODELS. H1 ALL hyperparameters are mine; the paper states none. Ridge = glmnet alpha = 0, lambda by 5-fold CV lambda.min. MLP = nnet, one hidden layer of 8 units, decay 1e-3, maxit 300, linout, MaxNWts 4000 (the paper says only 'multiple layers of interconnected neurons'). RF = ranger, 500 trees, mtry = floor(sqrt(#groups)), min.node.size 5, 1 thread. H2 the MLP target is standardised on the training window and the prediction mapped back to return units, so the three models combine on one scale; without it the 1e-3 weight decay collapses the output layer against ~1e-2 monthly returns. Paper silent. H3 set.seed(20250826 + slot) before each CV / MLP / RF fit and the same value as ranger's seed; one fit per model per month, no restarts, no outer ensemble. The paper is silent on seeds, restarts and ensembling. H4 regression task only. The paper also trains a classification task (rise/fall) whose precision / recall / F1 feed its STATIC weighting; that branch is not implemented. H5 labels are not winsorised (paper silent); the monthly label is the compounded return over (month_end[k], month_end[k+1]] using whatever trading days the stock had, so a mid-period delisting shortens the window and no minimum day count is imposed. H6 ADDED thresholds: a month needs >= 100 training rows and >= 20 scorable stocks, else it emits nothing.
(I) COMBINATION. I1 CELL CHOSEN: IC_Mean dynamic weighting WITH factor screening -- the paper's own best cell (results (2) and (3), Tables 4 and 6). The static evaluation-metric weightings (1/RMSE, 1/MAPE, Precision, Recall, F1) and the IC_Ratio weighting are NOT implemented. I2 L = 20 is read as 20 MONTHS. Algorithm 2 never gives the unit; section 3.2.1's parallel sentence says 'the rolling average of each evaluation metric over the past 20 trading months', and the only '20 trading days' usages in the paper are the IR factor definitions. I3 TIMING. My slot algebra makes Algorithm 2's literal window tau in [t-L, t-1] achievable with no look-ahead: the decision date for slot k is me[k], the label y(tau) is realised at me[tau+1], so IC(tau) for tau <= k-1 is fully observed at me[k]. The IC log is appended only one step after the prediction and every consumed row is hard-asserted on its realisation date. I4 Algorithm 2 line 1 starts at t = L+1 assuming all L ICs exist. A month that emitted no prediction produces no IC, so mu_IC is averaged over the ICs actually PRESENT in the trailing 20-month window (minimum 1 per model) rather than stalling for 20 months. I5 an IC observation requires >= 20 stocks with both a prediction and a realised label. I6 when S = sum(max(mu_IC, 0)) = 0, Algorithm 2 sets every weight to 0; no scores are emitted that month, so the simulator carries the previous holdings to the next scored month. Emitting a constant 0 score instead would hand the runner an arbitrary ranking.
(J) PORTFOLIO LAYER. J1 the paper never states a holding count, a position-weighting scheme, or long-only vs long-short: Algorithm 1 line 7 says only 'Form portfolio based on predicted returns', there is no portfolio-construction section, and Tables 2-4 report no holdings / weight / leg column. The only quantitative trace of leg structure is Table 4 reporting a POSITIVE Beta above 1 against the CSI 300, which is incompatible with a market-neutral long-short book and consistent with a long-only directional portfolio. The engine therefore emits FACTORS(Date, Ticker, Score) and the portfolio layer takes the harness fixed axis: top 25 by Score, equal-weight, monthly. The monthly rebalance IS the paper's ('the training and test windows are advanced by one month'). J2 no stock is dropped from the panel for missingness; if a stock-month still lacks a group score the group is filled with that slot's cross-sectional median, else 0.
(K) COST. K1 the paper's only cost statement is a 'total cost rate set at 0.3%' (section 3.1 Step 4, Algorithm 1 Input, Algorithm 1 line 8), with no one-way / round-trip split, no buy-sell split, no impact or slippage term and no reported turnover. Recorded as commission_paper = 0.003 and read as ROUND-TRIP. The harness charges sum(|dw|) * commission per rebalance, so passing 0.003 would charge 0.3% per side (0.6% round-trip at full turnover); the one-way equivalent of the paper's figure is 0.0015. Flagged, not silently converted. The grade is produced at the harness's own 15bps regardless.
(L) PIT NOTES. L1 a monthly Factor DB panel is consumed only if its reported as-of month EQUALS the requested month and its as-of date is <= the requested date; the connector otherwise substitutes the closest EARLIER month file, and that substitution is rejected rather than consumed as a stale cross-section. L2 training labels and IC observations each carry an explicit realisation date and the engine hard-stops if any of them postdates the decision date. L3 every rolling reducer is trailing-only (stats::filter(sides = 1), frollmean / frollsum, shift with positive n); there is no negative shift, no forward or rolling join, no manual future index, and no full-sample mean / sd / cov / min / max on any panel. L4 the feature set (which groups, which indicators, which survivors) is decided per decision month from slots [k-12, k] alone, never from the whole panel and never from an evaluation-window outcome (C1 / C14).
paper_original_form: A cross-sectional next-month expected-return forecast per stock: an IC_Mean-weighted combination of Ridge / MLP / Random Forest predictions, each model retrained monthly on a rolling 12-month panel of 8 entropy-weight-method-aggregated CNE5-style first-level factors (50 second-level indicators LASSO-screened to 37, preprocessed by industry-median imputation, 3xMAD, Z-score and industry+market-cap residual centering) over CSI 300 constituents, with the portfolio-formation step left unspecified ('Form portfolio based on predicted returns') and a 0.3% total cost rate.

source_paper.title: Combined machine learning for stock selection strategy based on dynamic weighting methods
source_paper.authors: Lin Cai, Zhiyang He, Caiya Zhang
